title: In deed and in truth (1 John 3:11–18)
hook: love not in word only but in deed

segments.voice: Yesterday, what manner of love, and your line was children of god. Which harsh name for yourself did you swap out? Day six hundred eighty-six.

A heart emoji takes half a second. A sympathy post takes ten. Driving across town with soup takes an afternoon. All three can be sincere. But only one of them is warm when it arrives. For days now, First John has circled love: old, new, the love that names believers children of God. Today he gets very practical. He reaches back to Cain and Abel, and then he asks a question about a bank account and a neighbor in need. Here a letter that can sometimes float comes down to earth.

In the King James Bible: "For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another." Then the counterexample, from the first pages of Genesis: don't be like Cain, who killed his brother. The writer goes further: whoever hates his brother is a murderer at heart. Hatred is the seed; Cain shows what it grows into. So what does love look like? Not a feeling first. A shape. "Hereby perceive we the love of God, because he laid down his life for us: and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren." For Christians, the cross is the measure of love. And then, right away, the writer brings it down from the heroic to the everyday. Laying down a life is rare. But: "whoso hath this world's good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him?" Bowels of compassion sounds odd to us. The Greek word means the inner organs, the gut, where feeling was felt. We still say a gut feeling, or it hit me in the stomach. The picture is of someone who sees a need, feels that tug inside, and shuts it off. Then the line this whole passage builds to: "My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth." In deed: something done. In truth: something real, not a performance. This week we've walked from the end of James into First John: pray for one another, what we have touched, God is light, the old new commandment, little children, what manner of love, and now, in deed and in truth.
screen: `HE LAID DOWN HIS LIFE FOR US.`
then, large: `IN DEED AND IN TRUTH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: do one loving deed. Settle, and breathe. Think of a need you've seen in the last week that tugged at you. Someone tired, someone short of money, someone lonely, someone sick. Remember the tug, the gut feeling. Notice if you shut it off, and why: busy, unsure, embarrassed. No blame. Now choose one small deed you could actually do about it. Not a feeling. Not a post. A deed. Picture yourself doing it, step by step, until you can see it clearly. If you pray, you can ask for the courage to follow through. The bell holds the time.
In deed and in truth. Love that does something real, not only words or the tongue: an open hand to a brother or sister in need.

segments.voice: Your line: not in word only. Today, do the deed you pictured, even a small version of it, before you post or say anything about it. Day six hundred eighty-six.

howItsDone: Christians organizing meal trains, collections and visiting sometimes quote 1 John 3:18, and churches read it alongside James 2 on faith and works.

fork.setup: you have plenty, and you see a friend in real need. you feel the tug. what does the letter ask?
options: send warm words and move on.
open your hand and help, in deed and in truth.
fork.reveal: "how dwelleth the love of God in him?" the writer asks of anyone who shuts up compassion. "let us not love in word... but in deed and in truth."

original.note: Greek: inner organs, the gut, and so compassion. the KJV renders it bowels of compassion.

trapdoor: what you thought: be nice to people.
what it means: love measured by a laid-down life, and brought down to an open hand for a neighbor in need.
what a scholar hears: splanchna, the gut as the seat of feeling, and Cain as the dark counterpoint to love from the beginning.
